page.mentor_intro: PrEP's problem is no longer whether it works but whether people can get it, stay on it, and be supported through the cycles of starting, stopping and restarting that real life imposes. Implementation science now dominates the literature: systematic reviews of best practices, global syntheses of provider barriers, and frameworks describing how programs must move from development and diffusion to genuine integration. Two populations remain systematically under-served — gay and bisexual men facing access disparities, and pregnant and postpartum women, for whom prevention is also child health.

teaching_points.claim: A qualitative systematic review identifies characteristics of best practices for increasing PrEP use and persistence, and maps research gaps in current PrEP interventions.
A global systematic review and meta-analysis quantifies health-care providers' awareness, willingness and key barriers to implementing PrEP.
PrEP implementation has moved through waves of development (2012–2015) and diffusion (2016–2018); reducing persistent disparities in access requires a next wave focused on integration of services.
Pregnancy is a critical window to elicit HIV vulnerability, offer testing, and provide PrEP for the pregnancy, postpartum period and future conception planning.

uncertainties: Which delivery models best sustain PrEP persistence through discontinuation-and-restart cycles is not established.
Provider-level barriers identified in global syntheses vary widely by health system, limiting generalisable solutions.
mcq_angles: PrEP continuum of care: indication, initiation, persistence, discontinuation, restart.

PrEP in pregnancy and breastfeeding: indications and counselling.

page.mentor_intro: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate with emtricitabine is the drug pair on which oral PrEP was built, and its clinical profile is unusually favourable: trial-level efficacy of 74–92% among participants with detectable drug levels, a safety record gathered across large prevention trials, and adverse events that are real but mostly manageable — nausea at initiation, small declines in renal function, and bone-density effects that matter mainly in younger patients. Knowing this safety architecture is what lets clinicians prescribe confidently and monitor selectively rather than reflexively.

teaching_points.claim: Prophylactic TDF-based regimens reduce the risk of HIV infection by 74 to 92% among participants with detectable drug levels, and available evidence supports PrEP efficacy when combined with other preventive methods.
Safety concerns are a recognised challenge in PrEP implementation, and dedicated reviews discuss the adverse-event profile and its management.
Adverse events observed in clinical trials of TDF/FTC for PrEP are documented in a dedicated drug-safety evaluation, informing monitoring practice.

uncertainties: Long-term (beyond trial follow-up) renal and bone effects of TDF-based PrEP in younger populations need ongoing surveillance.
How to individualise monitoring frequency for patients with borderline renal function is practice-dependent.
mcq_angles: Efficacy magnitude of TDF/FTC PrEP and the central role of adherence (detectable drug levels).
Adverse-effect profile: GI intolerance, renal tubular effects, bone density.

page.mentor_intro: The prognosis question in HIV has flipped completely: it is no longer 'how long' but 'how close to normal'. With modern ART, published life-expectancy estimates for people with HIV on treatment approach those of the general population, though a gap persists that depends on when treatment starts, baseline CD4, and health system context. The residual burden has also shifted — from AIDS-defining illness to non-AIDS comorbidity — which is why markers such as the CD4/CD8 ratio are being studied to flag patients whose immune dysfunction persists despite viral suppression. Late diagnosis remains the single most powerful determinant of a worse prognosis even after ART begins.

teaching_points.claim: A systematic review of published estimates finds life expectancy of HIV-positive adults on ART increasingly approaches that of the general population, though gaps remain by timing of initiation and setting.
Individuals first diagnosed with advanced HIV have higher mortality than those diagnosed earlier, even after starting ART, making early diagnosis the key prognostic lever.
The CD4/CD8 ratio and CD8+ T-cell count are being evaluated as prognostic markers for non-AIDS mortality in treated people living with HIV, beyond what CD4 count alone explains.

uncertainties: How much of the residual life-expectancy gap is attributable to persistent immune activation versus lifestyle and traditional risk factors.
Whether CD4/CD8-ratio-guided interventions actually improve non-AIDS outcomes is unproven.
mcq_angles: Life expectancy of treated HIV versus the general population, and what modifies the gap.
Advanced HIV at diagnosis as a prognostic determinant despite ART.
Non-AIDS mortality and emerging markers (CD4/CD8 ratio, CD8 count).
Prognosis counselling: what to tell a newly diagnosed patient.
case_hooks: A newly diagnosed 30-year-old asks 'will I live a normal life?'; construct an evidence-based answer.

page.gaps: Quantitative life-expectancy figures by region and subgroup, and smoking/ lifestyle adjustment data, are not extractable from the retained abstracts; verify against the full systematic review before approval.

page.mentor_intro: HIV testing technology has quietly revolutionised the epidemic's control: the evolution from antibody-only assays through fourth-generation antigen/antibody tests to nucleic-acid detection has compressed the window period dramatically, and each advance matters most in acute infection, when viral load and transmissibility peak. Universal screening is now recommended for all adolescents and adults at least once, with repeat testing for those at risk — yet testing is also where the cascade leaks, since a reactive test that is not confirmed and linked achieves nothing.

teaching_points.claim: The US Preventive Services Task Force recommends universal HIV screening at least once for adolescents and adults aged 15 to 65, with additional screening for higher-risk patients, reflecting recent changes in testing technology.
Appropriate screening is the cornerstone of HIV-related care, with several recent changes in testing technology and screening recommendations.

The earliest months of HIV infection carry high viral loads and elevated transmissibility; narrowing the window between acquisition and a reactive test, followed by rapid ART linkage, is the key transmission-prevention opportunity.

uncertainties: Optimal screening intervals for higher-risk groups beyond 'at least annual' vary by guideline.
Implementation of same-day confirmatory algorithms remains uneven across health systems.

page.mentor_intro: Hodgkin lymphoma is the model of a curable malignancy: a disease whose modern combination chemotherapy and risk-stratified radiotherapy transformed survival from months to the great majority of patients cured. It divides into classical Hodgkin lymphoma — with its nodular sclerosis, mixed cellularity, lymphocyte-depleted and lymphocyte-rich subtypes — and nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease, which behaves differently enough to manage as a related but distinct entity. Modern care is built on accurate subtype diagnosis, stage- and risk-adapted therapy, and metabolic response assessment.

teaching_points.claim: Hodgkin lymphoma comprises two distinct entities — classical HL and nodular lymphocyte-predominant HL — with classical subtypes including nodular sclerosis, mixed cellularity, lymphocyte depletion and lymphocyte-rich.

Classic Hodgkin lymphoma has an incidence of approximately 85,000 patients globally per year with a predilection for adolescents and young adults aged 15–39, and outcomes have improved dramatically since the introduction of combination chemotherapy.
Contemporary management rests on diagnosis, risk-stratification and stage-adapted therapy, updated in the 2025 review of the field.

uncertainties: How to minimise late toxicity (cardiac, second malignancy) while preserving cure rates in young, cured populations.
Optimal management of nodular lymphocyte-predominant HL, which diverges from classical HL pathways, is less standardised.
mcq_angles: WHO classification: classical subtypes versus nodular lymphocyte-predominant HL.
Stage and risk-group assignment driving therapy choice.
ABVD lineage and role of PET-adapted response assessment.

page.mentor_intro: More than 80% of advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma is now cured, so the frontline question has become how to escalate for those at highest risk of relapse without over-treating everyone else. Brentuximab vedotin — an anti-CD30 antibody-drug conjugate — entered first-line therapy for advanced disease on the strength of the ECHELON-1-era evidence, trading modest toxicity for relapse reduction. Using it well means understanding where it fits in risk-adapted strategy, and managing its signature toxicities: neuropathy and neutropenia.

teaching_points.claim: More than 80% of patients with advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma are cured with contemporary approaches; the challenge is escalating therapy for high-risk patients while de-escalating safely for lower-risk patients.

Treatment intensity adaptation to early metabolic response assessed by PET/CT has been a cornerstone of risk stratification in advanced-stage HL, and monoclonal antibodies are being incorporated into first-line classical HL treatment.
Brentuximab vedotin is effective and well tolerated in classical Hodgkin lymphoma and was initially FDA-approved after failure of autologous transplant or at least two prior chemotherapy lines.

Neutropenia, including febrile neutropenia, is a significant frontline toxicity of advanced HL therapy, with risk differing across regimens and patient characteristics, and guideline-based management principles apply.

uncertainties: Whether PET-adapted de-escalation can spare toxicity without sacrificing cure is being refined trial by trial.
Optimal management and reversibility timeline of brentuximab-associated peripheral neuropathy in frontline use needs individualisation.
mcq_angles: CD30 targeting and brentuximab vedotin's mechanism as an antibody-drug conjugate.

page.mentor_intro: Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer is the commonest breast cancer biology and the one in which the gap between early and advanced disease is most stark: adjuvant endocrine therapy converts early disease into high cure rates, yet advanced HR+ disease, though indolent, remains incurable and lethal. Modern management layers CDK4/6 inhibition onto endocrine backbone in the advanced setting, hunts resistance mechanisms — above all ESR1 mutations from aromatase-inhibitor pressure — and is now deploying PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway inhibitors for tumours carrying those aberrations. Sequencing these tools intelligently is the core clinical skill.

teaching_points.claim: Breast cancer is highly heterogeneous, and treatment strategies vary by molecular features including hormone receptor and HER2 status.

Adjuvant endocrine therapy has improved outcomes in early-stage HR-positive disease, with choice of agent driven by menopausal state, patient preference and side effects, and molecular profiling enabling tailoring.
Dysregulation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway is increasingly recognised as a key driver in HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer, and inhibitors of this pathway are an established therapeutic class.
ESR1 mutations are a common mechanism of acquired resistance to aromatase-inhibitor estrogen deprivation in metastatic HR-positive disease and are an emerging biomarker guiding therapy selection.

uncertainties: Optimal sequencing after CDK4/6 inhibitor progression (PI3K/AKT/mTOR agents, SERDs, ADCs) is evolving rapidly.
Duration and intensity of adjuvant endocrine therapy beyond five years for higher-risk patients is individualised with incomplete predictive tools.
mcq_angles: Endocrine agent selection by menopausal status (tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors, ovarian suppression).

page.mentor_intro: Menopausal hormone therapy has lived two lives: routine preventive panacea until the Women's Health Initiative abruptly ended that era in 2002, and since then, a symptom-targeted treatment whose risk-benefit calculus depends heavily on when it is started, how it is delivered, and who is asking. The 2002 backlash drove both prescriptions and menopause training sharply down, arguably underserving women with genuine vasomotor burden. Modern guidance — including the 2022 North American Menopause Society position statement — restores hormone therapy as the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms while retaining clear cautions about timing, duration and individual risk.

teaching_points.claim: The 2022 NAMS position statement updates the 2017 version through an expert advisory panel review, defining current indications and cautions for hormone therapy.
Since the 2002 Women's Health Initiative initial results, treatment for menopausal symptoms and practitioner training in menopause management have sharply declined.

uncertainties: Whether the 'timing hypothesis' — cardiovascular benefit when started near menopause — holds at trial level remains debated.
Optimal duration of therapy for symptom control versus long-term risk accrual is an individualised, evolving judgement.

page.mentor_intro: Hormone therapy for cardiovascular prevention is one of medicine's most instructive reversals. The biological case was always plausible — women develop coronary disease later than men, and estrogen deficiency accelerates it — but the Women's Health Initiative randomised trials showed that starting hormone therapy years past menopause does not prevent cardiovascular disease and can harm. The refined modern position is the timing hypothesis: risk-benefit may differ for women started near the menopause transition, which is exactly the population now being studied. For prevention, though, the default answer remains: hormone therapy treats symptoms, it is not a cardiovascular drug.

teaching_points.claim: Cardiovascular benefits of estradiol are documented in reproductive-aged women, while accelerated CVD development follows loss of ovarian estradiol and progesterone production.
A scientific statement on the menopause transition examines whether the MT contributes to the increase in coronary heart disease risk and the implications for timing of early prevention.

An umbrella review comprehensively summarises the benefits and harms of menopausal hormone therapy across diverse health outcomes, reflecting persistent uncertainty about its overall impact on women's health.
The Women's Health Initiative randomised trials — enrolling over 160,000 postmenopausal women — remain the definitive evidence base informing clinical practice on hormone therapy's health effects.

uncertainties: Whether early-initiation MHT around the menopause transition reduces cardiovascular endpoints awaits dedicated trial evidence.
Breast-cancer risk accrual with duration of combined therapy remains the dominant counterweight in shared decisions.
mcq_angles: WHI findings: why hormone therapy is not used for cardiovascular prevention.

page.mentor_intro: Hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia are the commonest fatal hospital infections, and HAP in particular is now the leading cause of death from nosocomial infection in critically ill patients. Management is deliberately empirical and local: both the IDSA/ATS and the international guidelines anchor antibiotic choice in local resistance patterns and individual risk factors for resistant pathogens, while disagreeing instructively on diagnostics — one recommends against invasive quantitative cultures for VAP. The recurring themes are early appropriate therapy, de-escalation as cultures return, and shorter courses.

teaching_points.claim: The 2016 IDSA/ATS guideline provides management standards for HAP and VAP while explicitly leaving room for physician judgement in individual cases.
International ERS/ESICM/ESCMID/ALAT guidelines incorporate randomised-trial evidence published after the prior European guidance on epidemiology, diagnosis, empiric treatment and response assessment.

Two recent major VAP guidelines recommend basing initial empiric antibiotics on local resistance patterns and individual risk for resistant pathogens, and one recommends against invasive diagnostic techniques with quantitative cultures.
HAP is currently the main cause of death from nosocomial infection in critically ill patients worldwide, despite widely used management guidelines.

uncertainties: Invasive versus non-invasive diagnostic strategies for VAP remain a genuine guideline divergence.
